senses.definition: A device that uses stored chemical energy to push electric charge around a circuit.
senses.example: A battery lets the flashlight work without plugging it into a wall.

senses.definition: A substance that lets charged particles move through it, such as the substance between the ends of a battery.
senses.example: Moving particles inside the electrolyte help the battery work.

senses.definition: An electric circuit with its parts arranged along one path for current.
senses.example: The lamps in a series circuit both go out if one place in the path breaks.

senses.definition: An electric circuit that gives current more than one path to follow.
senses.example: One lamp in a parallel circuit can be off while another keeps shining.

senses.definition: Electric charge that has collected somewhere rather than flowing steadily through a path.
senses.example: Static electricity made the balloon pull toward the wall.

senses.definition: A magnet that gets its magnetic field from flowing electricity.
senses.example: The crane’s electromagnet could let go of metal when its power was switched off.

senses.definition: A device that uses a changing magnetic field between coils of wire to change electric voltage.
senses.example: The transformer lowers the voltage for use in the building.

senses.definition: A device that opens part of a circuit automatically when more current flows than it is made to carry.
senses.example: When too much current flowed, the circuit breaker opened the path.

senses.definition: A small electronic part that gives off light when electricity flows through it in the proper direction.
senses.example: A green LED lights up when the speaker is charged.

senses.definition: A device that stores energy by keeping opposite electric charges apart.
senses.example: A camera flash can take a quick burst of energy from a capacitor.

senses.definition: A hard mineral. A piece cut to the right shape can vibrate at a regular rate in a clock.
senses.example: The watch has a quartz crystal to help it count time.

senses.definition: A movable part near the outer end of an airplane wing that helps tip the plane to one side.
senses.example: Moving the ailerons changes how much each wing lifts.

senses.definition: A movable part that helps turn the nose of a boat or an aircraft from side to side.
senses.example: The rudder can swing one way or the other at the back of the plane’s tail.

senses.definition: Water that flows off land or buildings instead of staying where it fell or soaking into the ground.
senses.example: Runoff followed the edge of the road into a drain.

senses.definition: A machine-readable pattern that stands for numbers or other information.
senses.example: The shop scanner read the barcode on a juice bottle.
